To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the inclusion of spin effects in gravitational-wave searches is not currently justified, and that it is not clear that such an inclusion will be justified in the near future, even though spin effects may have an important influence on the gravitational waves produced by some binary systems.

the phenomenological templates we developed for this project have comparable performance to the stationary phase templates currently in use by LIGO and that the false alarm rate of the phenomenological templates is not yet sufficiently low for use in a detection pipeline.

(i) the use of phenomenological templates does not increase the sensitivity of searches for coalescing binaries with spinning components; (ii) the use of stationary phase templates is adequate for the detection of coalescing binaries in LIGO and Virgot data, and (iii) the false alarm rate of searches using stationary phase templates can be reduced by using the method of "time slides."

the development of new methods for detecting compact binary coalescences with gravitational-wave detectors.

we found that a template bank using phenomenological templates was no more effective than a bank using stationary phase templates.
the use of spin templates does not improve the search for compact binaries.
